name: Hsü Kan
bio: Hsü Kan is dated by Giles to the 2nd and 3rd centuries AD, the last years of the Han dynasty. His poem here speaks in the voice of a wife whose husband is away.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: An Absent Husband
poems.author: Hsü Kan
poems.text:
Floating clouds that swim in heaven above
Bear on your wings these words to him
I love
Alas, you float along nor heed my pain,
And leave me here to love and long in vain!
I see other dear ones to their homes return,
And for his coming shall not I too yearn?
Since my lord left — ah me, unhappy day! —
My mirror's dust has not been brushed away;
My heart, like running water, knows no peace,
But bleeds and bleeds forever without cease.
